transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I've just been having a little bit of trouble keeping things organized lately? It's probably not a huge deal, I know everyone gets a little messy sometimes, but I'm trying to balance my schoolwork and this little accessories shop I run. And I just feel like I can't quite get them organized at the same time. 

My craft supplies, the receipts, due dates, and all my assignment notes... they kind of just end up in these piles everywhere. And then I just look at them and I don't really know what to do first. I'm trying my best to stay on top of it, I really am. I hope I'm explaining that okay. Does that make sense as a reason to come in?
Thinking back, did you have similar struggles with organization, focus, or finishing tasks when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that's only become a problem recently?

Um, well, I guess it's not entirely new? I hope it's okay to bring this up, but my mom actually still has some of my old elementary school notes from my teachers. They're mostly really positive, I promise! But... they did say I was, um, always getting out of my seat. And I guess I had a bit of a habit of talking before I was actually called on? 

I think I was just really eager to participate, you know? Like, the teachers noted that I understood the work just fine, but I would kind of rush through all the group activities really fast. I really wasn't trying to be disruptive or a bad student or anything, I just had a lot of enthusiasm, I think. Does... does that count as what you're asking about? I hope I'm answering your question right.
These days, do you notice yourself feeling restless, needing to move around a lot, or having trouble staying seated for long periods, like during classes or work at your shop?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm restless, exactly. I mean, I do like to stay active! But, um, I guess during really long classes, or if I have a longer meeting with a vendor for my shop... I do find myself getting up a bit. 

I always have a good reason, though! Like, I'll realize I need to check my inventory box, or I'll remember I really should refill my water bottle, or I'll just take a quick walk to the hallway to stretch my legs. I try really hard not to bother anyone when I do it, I promise. It's just... after a while, staying in the chair almost feels, um, kind of impossible? Like my body just really needs to do something else for a second. 

I hope it's okay to admit that. I know I should probably just sit still, but I figure it's better to get up and be productive, right? Does... does that sound like what you mean by needing to move around?
Do you often find yourself blurting out answers or interrupting others in conversations before they've finished speaking?

Oh, um... I try really hard to be a good listener, I promise! But, well... sometimes, especially in, like, group critiques or class discussions? I do kind of... jump in a little early. 

I just get so invested in what we're talking about, and I'll think I know exactly where their thought is going. So I'll just jump in with my answer before the other person is actually done talking. 

I always feel so embarrassed right after I do it, though. Because I'll realize I just totally guessed what they were going to say, and I basically interrupted them to do it. I swear I'm never trying to be rude or talk over anyone! I just get a little too eager to share or agree with them, I think. Does... does that make sense? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible classmate.
Do you often find yourself losing focus partway through a task, forgetting important steps, or misplacing things you need for school or your shop, even when you're trying to pay close attention?

Um... I really try my best to stay on top of everything, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm careless or anything! But, well... I guess sometimes, if a teacher or, like, someone from a vendor meeting gives me a few steps to do at once... I usually jump right in and handle the first part really well! 

But then... um, later on, I'll find out I somehow skipped something important. Like, I might forget to attach a form they asked for, or I'll realize I didn't finish the very last part of an order note. 

It's never on purpose, I swear! I just get so enthusiastic about getting that first part done that the rest kind of... slips my mind, even when I'm trying really hard to pay attention. I always make sure to apologize and fix it as soon as I realize, though! Does... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples.

Would you say these organization and focus difficulties have actually caused real problems for you, like missed deadlines, lost income, or conflicts with teachers or vendors, both at school and in your shop?

Um, well... I really try not to let things get that far, I promise! I always want to be super reliable for everyone. But... I guess, if I'm being totally honest... it has caused a little bit of trouble lately. 

I feel really awful admitting this, but... because I keep getting mixed up, I actually missed some required steps for my program. It wasn't because I didn't care, I swear! But now... well, my financial aid is kind of at risk. I'm working really, really hard to talk to the office and fix it, though! 

And with my shop... there aren't any big conflicts or anything like that! But I have noticed that the people I work with on shop projects have started... well, depending on me a little less. Like they might just handle the important parts themselves instead of asking me to do it. 

It makes me feel so guilty, because I never want to let anyone down. I'm really trying to get better organized so they know they can count on me again. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely irresponsible... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

This supports combined presentation ADHD rather than predominantly inattentive or hyperactive subtype.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient endorses multiple symptoms from both the inattentive domain (losing focus mid-task, forgetting steps, misplacing task components, disorganization) and the hyperactive-impulsive domain (difficulty remaining seated, restlessness, blurting out answers, interrupting others) that have been present since childhood (documented via elementary school teacher notes describing out-of-seat behavior and talking out of turn) and persist into adulthood. Symptoms occur across two or more settings (school/academic program and her shop/work with vendors), and she has clear functional impairment in both domains—financial aid jeopardy due to missed program requirements and diminished trust/reliance from shop collaborators. The combination of significant, persistent symptoms in both symptom clusters supports the Combined Presentation (F90.2) rather than a purely inattentive (F90.0) or purely hyperactive-impulsive (F90.1) subtype.
